newsitem.title: DENMARK: FLS Industries sees 1997 profits up.
newsitem.headline: FLS Industries sees 1997 profits up.

text.p: Danish cement and engineering group FLS Industries A/S said on Tuesday it expected 1997 profits higher than those in 1996, which themselves showed a sharp rise from the year before.

The forecast came in the group's 1996 annual report, which announced 1996 pre-tax profits up to 951 million crowns from 566 million in 1995 and net profit of 655 million crowns, compared to 412 million the year before.
It said that its success resulted from focusing on areas where it was an actual or potential market leader and selling of units with no such potential.

"Most of the group's companies have increased their geographical market coverage and therefore become more international and less dependent on economic developments in individual markets," the report added.

The result was well above analysts' average expectations of a profit before tax of 735 million crowns, but had no immediate effect on the share price, which was still untraded at Friday's closing 820 crown level 30 minutes after the report was issued.
FLS said that it expected increased competition, both from other international companies and at local level, but was nevertheless bullish about 1997.
"We expect in 1997 increased activity and revenues from most of the group's companies compared to 1996. The FLS group expects in 1997 to achieve an economic result that is better than 1996," it said.
It proposed raising the 1996 dividend to 16 percent, from 1995's 12 percent. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +4533969650
